newsitem.title: CHINA: HK sets "national security" rules to limit protest.
newsitem.headline: HK sets "national security" rules to limit protest.

text.p: Hong Kong, recently reunified with China, handed police discretionary powers on Friday to ban protests or political groups on grounds of "national security".

The government announced guidelines defining "national security". They allow the chief of police to ban gatherings if they threaten China's "national security", preach independence for Tibet or Taiwan, or cause a public disturbance.
The latest development came after another government move that froze a set of labour rights laws, drawing strong criticism from labour groups at home and abroad.
Hong Kong was a British colony for 156 years until July 1, when China resumed sovereignty over the territory, turning it into a quasi-autonomous special capitalist region.
Friday's statement said the police chief could also, if he "reasonably believes" it necessary, ask Hong Kong's security chief to cancel the registration of a society on grounds of national security.
By defining national security, the guidelines elaborated on curbs contained in new laws on registration of societies and on public order enacted 18 days ago.
